19.3 Promotion of Solar Water Heating System in domestic sector by providing
rebate on electricity bills to the users of solar water heater: extension of
rebate to Group Housing Societies.( Sales Circular No. U- 03 /2010)

The Nigam has issued instructions vide S.C No.U -08/2007 memo no. Ch. 69/SS -
429/COE dated 01.02.2007 for promotion of solar water heating system as a measure
to conserve electrical energy.
  Recently, apartment culture has developed in the state and a considerable
population in urban areas is now shifting to multistoried apartments/group housing
societies. After considering the needs of the residents in the group housing societies,
the State Govt. has decided to extend the rebate on electricity bills, presently available
to individual households to the Groups Housing Societies as well. In this matter,
approval of the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC) has also been
obtained vide their memo no. 3159/HERC/T-87-V-III dated 06.01.2010. The rebate to
the Group Housing Societies will be provided as per following guidelines.
1.  In case, individual system are installed in the Group Housing
 Societies, rebate in electricity bills may also be admissible @
 Rs. 100/ - per month for 100 liters system, @ Rs. 200/ - per month
 for 200 liter system and @ Rs. 300/ - per month for system of 300
 liters_and above capacity for a period of 3 years by UHBVN.
2.  In cases, where it is not possible to install individual systems and
 therefore combined systems are installed, the capacity of the
 system per flat may be calculated on pro -rata basis and the above
 incentive shall be admissible only if per flat 100 lpd or above
 capacity is installed in accordance with HAREDA guidelines issued
 vide memo no. DRE/HAREDA/2009/4341-64 dated 22.10.2009
3.  In such cases, the managing committee of the Group Housing
 Society will pass a resolution for installation o f solar water heating
 systems and apply for the incentive to the Director – HAREDA with
 a copy to the Addl. Deputy Commissioner -cum-Chief Project Officer
 office along with a list of the members, their identity proofs and
 invoice for the proposed system . The society will have the liberty to
 install the solar water heating systems either from the firms on the
 HAREDA rate contract or from the supplier of their own choice
 provided it is BIS/MNRE/GOI approved.

Page | 635

4.  After issuance of the installation/commissi oning report as per
 guidelines contained in the HAREDA memo no.
 DRE/HAREDA/2009/4341-64 dated 22.10.2009, the Group
 Housing Society will apply for rebate in electricity bill to the
 Additional Deputy Commissioner-cum-Chief Project Officer office  along
with members list and their electricity connection number and  per flat
capacity installed worked out on pro-rata basis. Thereafter,  the ADC -cum-CPO
will forward the application to the power utilities  for grant of rebate under
intimation to the Director, HAREDA.
  S.C No.U-08/2007 is amended to the above extent.

19.4 Directions for efficient use of energy and its conservation in the State of
Haryana( Sales Circular No. U-  41/2016)

  Kindly refer to S.C. No. U-54/2005 dated 19.10.2005 issued in compliance
to the Renewable Energy Department Notification No. 22/52/2005 -5P dated 29 thJuly,
2005 vide which as per clause ‘A’ the use of CFL in the Govt. Building / Govt. Aided
Institutions/ Board and Corporations/ Autonomous bodies was made mandatory.
  Now, in com pliance to the Renewable Energy Department Order No.
22/52/2005-5P dated The 29th June, 2016, the amended instructions are as under:-
“2. Mandatory use of Light Emitting Diode (LED) lamps/ tube lights and energy
efficient lighting:
1.  The use of incandescent lamps and purchase of new sodium vapour lamps
and lights having efficiency less than sodium vapour lamps by Government
Sector/ Government Aided Sector/ Boards and Corporation or
Autonomous bodies of Haryana is banned
2.  The use of Light Emitting Diode  (LED) lamps/ tube lights and energy
efficient lighting (More efficient then LED) shall be mandatory for all new:-
(i)  Central or State Government Offices and Public Sector Undertaking
Institutions or establishments located in the State of Haryana; and
(ii)  Electricity Consumers in Industrial, Commercial and Institutional sectors
having connected load of 30 kilowatt or above.
3.  In Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA) Sectors, Municipal
Areas, Areas developed by Haryana State Industr ial and Infrastructure
Development Corporation Limited (HSIIDC) or Industries Department, the
installation of Automatic Switching System (either solar based or timer
based) from dusk to dawn operation on existing as well as new Street
Lighting Rows, where common switch for more than twenty five lights is
required to be installed, shall be mandatory.

Power Utilities shall affect necessary modifications in the load demand
notices within two months time from the date of issue of this order to promote the use
of Light Emitting Diode (LED) lamps/ tube Lights or Energy Efficient Lighting (More
efficient than LED) system while releasing or sanctioning new connections and loads
The consumers of existing buildings under the category 2(i) shall replace
all the defective conventional bulbs, conventional tube lights, CFLs and T-5 tube lights
only by LED lamps / tube lights or energy efficient lighting system.
The consumers under the above category 2(ii) shall have to replace all
conventional bulbs, conventional tube li ghts, CFLs and T -5 tube lights in their
establishments with Light Emitting Diode (LED) lamps/ tube lights or energy efficient
lighting system within one year from the date of notification, at their own cost.

Note:-  The inspecting officer appointed by State Designated Agency under Energy
Conservation Act, 2001 (52 of 2001), may, therefore exercise power vested

Page | 636

under the Act for the purpose of compliance of these directions. In case of
non-compliance of these directions or on recommendation of Inspecting
officer, the power Utilities shall have the power to disconnect the electricity
connections after serving due notice after the expiry of the deadlines
mentioned above. The Executive Engineer (Distribution) of the Power
utilities shall be the enforcing authority of these directions and they shall
send quarterly progress reports in this regard to the Renewable Energy
Department, Haryana (copy of order dated 29.06.2016 is enclosed).
  Sales Circular No. U-54/2005 is amended to the above extent.
The above instructions may be brought to the notice of all concerned for
strict and meticulous compliance.

SECTION 20 MISCELLANEOUS SALES CIRCULARS

20.1 Using Nigam’s poles/laying of cable TV Network/ Internet wires/OFC cables
by Cable and Telecom Operators on the poles erected adjacent to Nigam’s
poles. (Sales Circular No. U- 07/2020)
Please refer to Sales Circular No. U-47/2007 dated 21.06.2007 vide which
instructions were issued that laying of cables for TV and internet network on Nigam’s
pole shall not be allowed.
2.  It has now came to the notice of the management that some Cable and
Telecom Operators are installing poles near Nigam’s LT/HT poles for l aying
cable/internet wires/OFC cables without adhering to safety measures and laid down
guidelines for installation of Cable/Internet wire/OFC cables. Following discrepancies
have been reported which may cause accidents: -
• There is no adequate clearance between the Nigam’s and Telecom
Operator’s poles.
• Length of the span between Telecom poles installed at various locations is
beyond the permissible limit. This may cause breakage of the cables.
• Hanging cables are giving shabby look to the surroundings.
• Horizontal distance between Telecom poles and Nigam’s poles is approx. 3
to 4 feet only.
• Vertical distance between Telecom poles and cables, conductor of Nigam
is approx 5 to 6 feet.
3.  The matter has been considered in view of various relevant provisions of
Communication and Connectivity Infrastructure Policy, 2017 of the Govt. of Haryana
and its time to time amendments and Regulations 58 to 61 of Central Electricity
Authority (Measures relating to Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations, 2010.
4.  Section 5.2 of CCIP-2017 stipulates as under: -
5.2  In so far as possible, any scheme for laying of overhead cables on poles
specifically erected for the purpose would be discouraged as the same tends
to interfere with the overhea d electricity distribution system apart from
disturbing the aesthetics of the eco system.
Therefore, the laying of overhead cables on poles should be discouraged if
the same tends to interfere with the overhead HT/LT lines, electricity distribution
system apart from disturbing the aesthetics of the eco system.
Wherever it is found that laying of overhead cable on pole by Telecom
operator would compromise with safety requirements with the Nigam’s HT/LT lines, it
should not be allowed.
5.  If any such occurre nce of installation without prior approval of Nigam is
observed, a notice attached herewith as Annexure -I be immediately served to the
concerned Telecom/Cable TV Operator with directions to remove unauthorized overhead
OFC/TV Network/Internet cable/Cable w ithin 15 days of the receipt of notice failing
which complaint shall be lodged with the concerned authorities as per Section 188 of
IPC, 1860 as well as Section 133 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
 The above instructions may be brought to the notice of all concerned for
strict and meticulous compliance.

20.2 Procedure for Permit to Work (PTW) to accelerate the process of issue &
cancellation of PTW (Sales Instruction No. U- 06/2020)

Instructions of issue and cancellation of permit to work (PTW) to the concerned
JE/AFM/authorized person through Whatsapp stands issued vide Sales Instruction No.
U-05/2018 dated 31.05.2018.

Page | 642

 2.  However, it has been continuously reported that HVPNL owned sub -
station staff doesn’t value these instructions creating difficulties for UHBVN officials for
taking PTW through Whatsapp in emergent situations. In order to bring co -ordination
between officials of both the Utilities, a meeting was held between Director/OP, UHBVN
and Director/T ech., HVPNL, Panchkula on 24.01.2020. As per recommendations,
updated process for issue and cancellation of PTWs to the concerned
JE/AFM/authorized person through Whatsapp is detailed as under:
i.  The procedure for issue and cancellation of PTW in -vogue shall remain in
practice (Annexure-II).
ii. In addition, PTW for 11 KV level only may be allowed to the concerned
JE/AFM/authorized person on Whatsapp message. The message should be
sent by the concerned JE/AFM/authorized person for issue of PTW along with
picture of filled PTW form (Annexure -III). The official shall ask for PTW in
writing mentioning the name of feeder duly filled and signed on the format of
this PTW book and the same shall be sent to the Sub -Station attendant
through Whatsapp. The sub-station attendant shall also fill-up the PTW book
and allow (duly signed) and shall rack out 11 KV VCB along with Caution
Notice. The S/Stn. incharge shall also post the picture of racked out VCB
along with picture of Caution Notice and allow PTW. The same procedure i s
to be followed for cancellation of PTW i.e. signed cancellation request by
authorized JE/AFM/authorized person through Whatsapp.
iii. The JE/AFM/Authorized person shall also indicate the name of feeder/line
crossing the feeder as a foot note on the PTW for which PTW has been applied.
In addition, the in-charge shall indicate whether the feeder crossings are safe
crossings or un -safe crossings. If un -safe, then he would take  PTW of that
feeder too. However, he will take measures in near future to make safe
distance so as to make both crossings as safe crossings.
iv. The JE/AFM/Authorized person shall have to submit (latest by next day) the
hard copy of PTW request to sub-station incharge for maintaining the proper
record otherwise he shall not be allowed to take PT W through Whatsapp
requisition.
v. Each page of the serial numbered PTW book shall be signed and issued by
SDO ‘OP’ concerned under proper acknowledgement.
vi. Before sending the requisition of PTW via Whatsapp, JE/AFM/authorized
person shall contact the sub-station attendant through  his official mobile
number and establish a dialogue in this regard.
3.  Other important measures suggested to avoid accidents: -
a) On the occasion of planned shutdown , the. JE-in-charge shall also ensure
switching off supply . from 1st H-Pole and shall also ensure for proper
maintenance & earthing of 1st H-Pole.
b) To further ensure the safety of man and machinery at least two video cameras
with DVR having one month memory should be installed in each sub-station.
c) To work on DT, the particular DT is to be isolated from both sides (HT & LT,) i.e
by opening GO Switch of DT & removing the RD fuses and to remove all the four
LT fuses . To work on LT line, remove all the four LT fuses at DT and to do
temporary earthing on both sides of LT line, where the official is to work.
d) JE-in-charge shall ensure whether the fault rectifying team is having voltage
detector device & other safety equipments. Execution be done after observing all
safety precautions.
e) Name of the feeder be indicated on Poles with plate or by painting on the Pole. It
is necessary where two or more lines are running in parallel.
f) Double supply plate should be fixed on HT/LT poles where required.
g) Planned shut downs for maintenance, erection of poles / sagging of ACSR,
installation/replacement of DTs etc. should be with the prior approval of
XEN/OP concerned.

Page | 643

4. Additional points
i. The official of the UHBVN is required to operate the GO switch of 1st H-pole of
the 11 KV feeder so as to ensure switching off supply and to do the earthing
of 1st H-pole before carrying out work after obtaining PTW. In order to have
better coordination, the same official of UHBVN should also sign the PTW
book in the HVPN s ub-station as and when PTW is taken in emergency on
behalf of authorized official to ensure that the proper trolley has been racked
out by the HVPN sub -station staff after the PTW has been sought through
Whatsapp by the authorized UHBVN official on his registered Mobile Number
as per instructions of the UHBVN.
ii. The name of the authorized official (sub -station wise as well feeder wise) be
circulated by concerned UHBVN officers and would be supplied again to the
respective HVPN officers giving the registered Mobile Numbers from where the
PTW would be sought through Whatsapp in case emergency PTW is required.
iii. The PTW for routine maintenance etc. would be obtained by the UHBVN
authorized official by visiting the HVPN sub-station.
iv. The details of the PTW book with serial numbers allotted to the authorized
UHBVN officials be also circulated by the UHBVN officers and would be
supplied to the concerned HVPN officers for reference and record.
v. The details of the 11 KV lines with multiple crossing be also identified and
circulated by the UHBVN officers, for which permit is also required whenever
permit is taken on that particular line to avoid accidents. The such list be also
supplied to the concerned HVPN officers.

1860 as well as Section 133 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.

20.4 Please refer to S.C. No. U -25/2016 vide which HERC (Electricity Supply
Code) Regulation, 2014 (HERC 29/2014) as amended vide HERC 1 st
Amendment dated 17 th Nov, 2014 and vide HERC order dated 16.12.2015
in case No. KNOW YOUR BILL” SCHEME (Sales  Instruction No. U-02/2021)

It has come into the notice that there are large number of billing and metering  related
issues/complaints of consumers due to which consumers face harassment. Accordingly,
the matter has been considered by the Nigam and it has been decided to launch the
“Know Your Bill” Scheme. The operational guidelines of the scheme are as under: -
12.On every Thursday, each SDO ‘OP’ will remain present in his/her office and
redress consumer grievances regarding electricity bills, metering, connection
dispute and tariff etc. from 10.00 AM to 02.00 PM. The complaints received
shall be resolved on the spot to the exte nt possible and the record shall be
maintained. Strict directions are hereby given to follow the instructions and
follow the schedule. On this day, SDOs (OP) shall review all pending
billing/metering complaints and ensure resolution of all complaints with in
timeline fixed by HERC.
13.Every Saturday has been fixed for holding village level Darbar in the
jurisdiction of Sub-Division by the SDO ‘OP’ from 10.00 AM to 01.00 PM. SDO
will take the sub-division team of JE/CA/Ledger Clerk/Consumer Clerk etc.
with him and redress the consumer grievances pertaining to electricity bill,
metering, connection dispute, tariff etc. on the spot to the extent possible.
14.In exceptional cases, if SDO is not present then senior most JE will hold the
village Darbar.
15.XEN ‘OP’ concern ed will head the village Darbar in any sub -division every
fortnight and similarly, SE ‘OP’ will hold village Darbar once in a month at
circle level.
16.Wide publicity through print media, social media/SMS should be given to the
scheme.
17.SE ‘OP’/XEN ‘OP’ shall ensure that no meeting is fixed during the time
SDO(OP)/XEN(OP) is occupied with the scheme.
18.Concerned staff should also remain present during the above schedule so that
site verification, if any required could be carried out on the same day.
19.If any activity is required at the end of Commercial Bank Office (CBO), prompt
action and redressal within 24hrs shall be ensured by XEN/CBO. And, if the
complaint requires higher time in redressal like involving binder
management, SDO(OP) shall inform the fact to the complainant.
20.All out efforts be ensured to redress the complaints on the spot itself or at the
most within 24 hours and intimation be sent to concerned SE ‘OP’/XEN ‘OP’.
21.SE(OP)/XEN(OP) shall review pendency of complaints in each sub -division
and ensure the success of this scheme.

20.6 Preventive measures to avoid accidents due to use of double supply (AP and
RDS) at a single premise (Sales Instruction No. U- 04/2019)

A fatal accident of Nigam lineman has come to the notice of management, which
occurred due to unauthorized use of double supply i.e. AP and RDS at a single premise
by using changeover switch. Time to time instructions are being issued by the Nigam to
disconnect such unauthorized double supply circuit to consumers. Sales Instruction
No.  U -30/2014 stipulates for the Dera Dhanies being provided supply through PAT
transformer that to avoid accidents, intermingling of supply and misuse by the
consumers, the existing RDS feeders/lines erected for providing RDS supply to the Dera
Dhanies be dismantled and material be returned to store.
  Therefore, an extensive drive becomes imperative at this stage to
disconnect all such double circuit connections. For the said purpose, following steps in
addition to aforesaid provisions of Sales Instruction No. U -30/2014 shall be taken
immediately: -
1. Checking of consumer premises in rural area where LT lines of both AP as
well as RDS feeder are crossing over the vicinity of consumer premises, should
be got carried out.
2. Armoured cable of LT line of AP feeder at places near the consumer premises
should be provided which will prevent taking of both AP as well as RDS feeder
supply by unscrupulous elements.

take appropriate safety measures and get it shifted as deposit work in their own interest.

20.8 Notification for requirement of Aadha ar under Section 7 of the Central

Aadhaar Act”) for Services/ benefits provided by Power Department. ( Sales

  State of Haryana has enacted an Act to seek Aadhaar from Citizens for
delivery of services, benefits and subsidies namely Haryana Aadhaar (Targeted delivery
of financial and other subsidies, benefits and services) Act 2017 passed and published
by the State Govt. on 23 rd March and 29 th March, 2017. As per the said Act, the
establishment of identity of an individual by seeking Aadhaar has been made a condition
for obtaining any subsidy, benefit or service for large  number of State Govt.  Schemes
which are funded out of the consolidated fund of the State.
2. Accordingly, in compliance of Haryana Aadhaar (Targeted delivery of financial
and other subsidies, benefits and services) Act 2017, it has been decided that Citizens
should be required to produce Aadhar for every service, benefit or  delivery of subsidy
by the Power Department.
  The above instructions may be brought to the notice of all
concerned for strict and meticulous compliance.

20.9 Scheduling of Power Banking facility for Non -Conventional Energy
Resource Producers under Haryana Renewable Energy Department
notification dated 23.11.2005 (Sales Circular No. U-  26/2017)

Haryana Govt. Renewable Energy Department issued policy for promoting
Generation of Electricity through Renewable En ergy Source notification No.
22/69/2005-5P dated 23.11.2005. As per clause no. 11 of the ibid policy, the
renewable energy resources based power producers can enter into banking
arrangement subject to terms & conditions defined here under.
2. Clause No. 11. BANKING:
HVPNL/ DHBVN/ UHBVN/ licensee is to permit electricity generated by
eligible producers to be banked. The banking facility shall be allowed for a period of one
year by the Licensee/ Utilities free of cost. However, withdrawal of banked power should
be allowed only during non -peak hours. If the banked energy is not utilized within a
period of twelve months from the date of power banked with the concerned power
utilities/licensee, it will automatically lapse and no charges shall be paid in lieu of such
power.
The wheeling charges shall be levied as per clause 9 of the ibid policy as
under:-
3. Clause No. 9. WHEELING CHARGES:
Licensee/ Utilities will undertake to transmit on its grid the power
generated by  power producers using non -conventional energy sources and make it
available to the producer for captive use or to a Third Party within the State  as  per
approved  tariff    including surcharge, additional surcharge, if any, notified by HERC
from  time  to  time.  If H.T./L.T. lines required to be laid beyond Licensee/ Utilities lines

Page | 653

for wheeling the power at any desired point, then the cost of the same shall have to be
borne by the promoter/power producer. In case, the power is to be sold to a third party,
the name of such party shall be indicated by the  power  producer at the time of making
an application in the prescribed form of Licensee/ Utilities. However, in respect of third
party sale, licensee/utilities would have preference over the power generated by the
power producers and third party sale would be allowed when the surplus power is not
being evacuated by the licensee/ utilities.
4. As such, the non conventional e nergy source producer who enters into the
banking arrangement with HPPC for transmitting the power for captive use within the
state at different location by another embedded consumer of UHBVN shall be dealt as
per the procedure given below:-
i) The accounting of the banked units shall be maintained by the Sr. AO/
Open Access as is being done for open access consumers.
ii) The SE/SO, UHBVN, Panchkula shall forward the slot -wise details
received from the O/o Chief Engineer/SO & Commercial, HVPN,
Panchkula to Sr. AO/ Open Access UHBVN, Rohtak for accounting of
banked power.
iii) The net power banked by the non conventional energy producer after
deduction of transmission losses as per details supplied by the HVPN in a
month shall be adjusted in the energy bill of the existing consumer who is
utilizing the banked power for captive use subject to the condition that
withdrawal of the banked power shall be allowed only during non peak
hours. If the banked energy is not utilized within a period of twelve months
from the date of power banked with the concerned power Utility/ licensee,
it will automatically lapse and no charges shall be paid in lieu of such
power.
iv) In case banked power is more than the consumption of embedded
consumer of UHBVN during non peak hours, the excess unadjusted power
shall be carried forward to the next month subject to the condition that If
the banked power is not utilized within a period of twelve months from the
date of power banked with the concerned power Utility/ licensee, otherwise
it will automaticall y lapse and no charges shall be paid in lieu of such
power.
v) The wheeling charges for use of distribution network shall be levied as per
rates determined by HERC, on the net exported banked power by the
generator in case power is injected on 11/33 KV level.  The rates of
wheeling charges shall be the rates as applicable at the time of net
export/injection of power for banking.
vi) The wheeling charges for use of distribution network shall also be levied
as per rates determined by HERC, on the net utilized banked power by the
embedded captive user unit in case power is drawn by it on 11/33 KV
level. The rates of wheeling charges shall be the rates as applicable at the
time of net utilization/drawl of banked power.
vii) The transmission charges as notified by HERC in its  tariff order issued
from time to time shall be made applicable on the net utilized imported
power for usage of transmission network and distribution network.
viii) The credit of banked units will be given only after pre-audit of the same by
Sr. A.O. (Open Access) in close coordination with Sr. AO (HPPC)/ Authority
maintaining such account.

20.10 Instructions regarding system for crossing of feeders in order to prevent
accidents (Sales Instruction No. U- 03/2017)
It has been observed that there are number of HT and LT line crossings in
the field due to which fatal / non- fatal accident occurs and these crossings also imposes
problem in the maintenance work.  To improve the existing infrastructure of HT and LT
line crossings so as to avoid fatal / non - fatal accidents , the following activities be
carried out in phase manner and the corrective work at dangerous crossings / crossings
at vital / vulnerable points be taken on priority:
Rerouting of 11 kV feeder to minimize the crossing with other feeder
All the field officers are advised to patrol all the 11 kV feeders and prepare record
of feeder crossings. The field officer should in first instance check whether this
crossing can be removed by rerouting the feeders or not. This should be our first
preference. If not, then  other steps to be taken for maintaining proper clearance
between feeders and ground clearance which are detailed as below:
Road crossing and guarding
1. As far as possible road crossing should be at right angle, but not less than
an angle of 60 degrees.
2. The Crossing span shall not be more than 80 % of the normal spans.
3. Cradle guarding be laid between the poles wherever there is road crossing
of power line or along the line. Carpet guarding be laid for Power Line
Crossing.
4. G.I. wire of 10 S.W.G. (British Stan dard Wire Gauge) for L.T. line and 8
S.W.G for 11 kV to 33 kV lines is used for guarding.
5. Every guard wire shall be connected with earth at each point at which its
electrical continuity is broken.
6. The first lacing should be at a distance of 750 mm from th e pole. Other
lacing are tied at a distance of 2 meter from each other.
7. The vertical distance between conductor and guarding in mid span should
be minimum 610 mm for L.T. and 1220 mm for H.T line.
8. The vertical distance between L.T. line guarding cross ar m and neutral
should be 610 mm (2 ft.) and the length of cross arms should be 750 mm
(2 ½ ft) .
9. The clearance between line and guarding cross arm for 11 kV and 33 kV
line should be 650 mm (2 ¼’) and 840 mm (2 ¾’) respectively.
10. Every guard wire for cross -connected system of guard wire shall have
sufficient current carrying capacity to ensure the rendering dead, without
risk of fusing of the guard wire or wires till the contact of any live wire has
been removed.
11. The minimum height between any guard wire and  live crossing conductor
should be 2.44 m upto 66 KV. However under the most adverse conditions
the minimum height between any guard wire and live crossing conductor
shall not be less than 1.5 meters.
Pole Accessories
i) Cross Arm, ii) Channel, iii) Stays, iv) Guarding, v) Barbed Wire (Anti -climbing
device), vi) Number plate, vii) Phase plate, viii) Circuit plate, ix) Danger Board etc.
a) Cross Arms: - Cross arm designed as per the formation of line i.e. vertical,
horizontal, or delta.
b) Channels: - Channels are used for mounting of Transformer, G.O. switch,
L.A., guarding etc. on pole.
c) Stays: To avoid pole bending.
d) Guarding: - To avoid snapping of conductor on ground/ another line

Page | 655

e) Barbed wire: - To obstruct the persons from climbing on the pole. Fixing o f
anti-climbing device is mandatory.
Barbed wire to be used as below:
Line Ground Clearance Barbed Wire Span
H.T Line 2134 ( 7 ft) 1220 mm (4ft)
L.T Line -do- 610 mm (2 ft)
f) Number plate: - Number plate should be fixed on every pole or number
should be painted. It facilitates attending breakdown by giving proper
address.
g) Phase plate: - On cut point of H.T. line or specific distance poles or tapping
poles, Red, Yellow and Blue phase plates are fixed.
h) Circuit Number: -When there is double circuit on a tower or pole, a circuit
number should be written on number plate. Hence fixing of number plate
should be done carefully. If wrong circuit number plate is fixed, permit will
be issued wrongly which may cause accident. Confirm the circuit at
orientation, and start fixing of the number plates at a right side.
i) Danger Board: - Danger Board should be fixed on every H.T. pole at following
points.
i) Danger Board of every road side pole should face the road.
ii) Danger Board should be on both side poles at Road crossing, Telephone
crossing, Power line, Railway, River crossing.
iii) Up to ½ K.M. on both sides of village or city
j) Name Plate of Feeder: When two feeders are crossing each other, Name plate
be affixed or Name be painted on each feeder.

Road Crossing

20.13 Protocol for Roles & Responsibilities of officers and officials at various level
for monitoring of online AMR of 11 kV feeders, DTs & HT consumers data
for proper energy auditing (Sales Instruction No. U- 01/2016)

Regular monitoring of online data of feeders as well as DTs is very  essential for taking
necessary planning and corrective actions besides the important task of energy auditing.
Lack of monitoring of data will ultimately result in all infrastructure becoming
redundant and nonfunctional.

Page | 661

  Since DCU/Modems installed on 11 KV Feeders and DTs are spread over
the vast area of the Town/Substation, it is imperative that the regular upkeep of this
infra is essential for online availability of complete AMR data. Apart from it, any
incremental changes (Delta Changes) in network like addition of DTs, New Feeders, LT
Lines, Reorientation of LT/HT lines need to be captured for updation in GIS database
and provision of metering of all such new points with communication set up is very
essential for accurate feeder as well as DT level energy auditing.

be reported, executed, monitored at different levels  and responsibilities of various

20.14 Reason for damage of transformer above 200 KVA (Sales Instruction No. U-
07/2016)
Transformer damage is a  routine process in the field.  It is observed that proper
monitoring of damage rate of transformers is not being done resulting into increase of
damage rate.
The matter has been reviewed and decided that
• As and when any transformer of 200 KVA is damage then it would be the duty
of concerned SDO/OP to inform about damage of transformer to Chief
Engineer/ OP within 6 hours and detailed investigation report is submitted
to Chief Engineer/OP along with the reason of damage.
• When any transformer having capacity more than 200 kVA is damaged then
it should be ensured that concerned XEN/OP informs damage of transformer
to Director (Operation), UHBVN, Panchkula within 6 hours on telephone and
e-mail, detailed investigation report is also submitted to Director(Ope ration),
UHBVN, Panchkula along with the reason of damage.
It is further clarified that transformer should be replaced as per prevailing instructions
of the Nigam

20.15 Clarification in the matter on   applicability of NDS  tariff  on residential
premises  used by   professional  for  advisory  purposes. (Sales Circular No.
U-41/2014)

Page | 663

Please refer to  Sale Circular  No.  U-30/2013 dated 05.07.2013, vide which schedule of
tariff of supply  of electricity  for  FY-2013-14 was  circulated .
Now, in  compliance to the order of the  HERC  in case  no. HERC/
PRO-22 of  2014 dated  22.07.2014. it  has  been clarified  that   tariff  payable  for the
energy  consumed  in the  year  2013-14 would be  as provided  in the   tariff order  for
FY- 2013-14 i.e  the  residential premises  used by the  professionals  like  lawyers,
Doctors , Professional  Engineers , Chartered  Accountants  etc   who use  the  space  ‘
occasionally’  in furtherance  of their professional  activity  in their residences, shall  be
charged  at the  domestic  tariff. The lawyers, doctors, professional  engineers and
chartered  accountants  , who carry  on their professional  activities  in their  residences
,  ‘ regularly’  or the office  is situated  in any commercia l  place  or market  will be
charged under  non  domestic category. ( for   more  clarity,  the  order of the HERC
dated  22.07.2014 may be  consulted  on   herc.gov.in).
   Sales Circular No. U- 30/2013 is amended to the above extent.
20.16 Construction of electric   lines (Sales  Instruction No. U- 25/2014)

Please refer to  S. I No. U- 21/2014  dated  19.09.2014  vide which the  directions  issued
bythe HERC memo no. 2061-2064/ HERC /T dated 27.08.2014   i.e   Regulation  2010
of  Central Electricity  Authority  (Technical  Standards  for Construction  of  the
Electrical  Plants and  Electric  line) and   guidelines  to  be followed in the  execution of
works of  construction  of  electric lines were   circulated . i.e
1. The  electric lines shall   be constructed  strictly  as  per the  Central
Electricity  Authority  ( Technical Standards  for  Construction  of
Electrical  Plants  and  Electric  Lines ) Regulations  ,  2010.
2.  The electric line  shall be  close to  a road  for approach  during
construction  and ease  of  maintenance.
3.   The notification issued  by the  licensees for informing  the public  about
the  erection of new  lines shall also  include the  following  information.
a)  Name of  the  villages  through which the  line  is to pass.
b)  Kila  number and  khasra  number  of the land  through  wh ich the
line   is to pass.
4.  Besides  issue  of  notification , there should  be a  munadi  by the  beat
of the drum in the  villages through  which the line  is to pass  so that the
land  owners  are well   aware  about the  same  and can   raise  objection
, if  any.
5.  While  constructing  new   electric  line through  the   agriculture  fields ,
poles/ structures  may  be placed  at the  boundary / maind of the field ,
as  far as possible , so that  the farmers  do not   find  any difficulty  in
ploughing  their fields.
6.   In case  an electric line  is already  existing  in an  agriculture  fields  (s)
and  a new  line   is proposed  to be erected  in the same  field (s), the new
line be erected  on the same route  as of the  existing  line by replacin g
the  existing  poles/  structures  with multi – circuit  towers  subject  to
feasibility  . All expenses  in this  regard  shall be   borne  by the  licensee.
7. In case  construction  of a pole / structure  is objected  by the  land  owner
at the  initial  stage  i.e  while  digging  of the land, the matter  may be
amicably settled  so as  to avoid  litigation , expenditure  towards  litigation
and delay  in the completion of work.
8.  The cases of payment   of compensation and other  disputes  between  the
owner of the land  and the    licensee,  if any,  should  be decided
expeditiously by the  competent authority   under the  relevant  rules /
laws.

Now, the  matter  has been  reconsidered  and   decided that :-

Page | 664

9. The new electric  lines , if  to be erected  in the agriculture  fields, be
constructed  during  the  period  when there is no standing  crop  in
the  field,  so that  damage  of crop  vis -a- vis  payment  of
compensation  to the  farmers  is avoided.

20.18 Reporting of feeder breakdown to call centre (18001801615) (Sales
Instruction No.U-06/2014)
It has  come to the notice  of the management that whenever a consumer  registers his
complaint  at the call centre of UH/DH  regarding  failure of his supply, the call centre
could not  intimate the consumer  regarding the position of the  supply failure of  the
entire  effected feeder or his  personal complaint.
  To overcome this problem and to have better consumer satisfaction,  it
has been  decided as under:-
1.   The sub- station from where the  33 KV  / 11 KV feeder are emanating,
 they have to  immediately intimate regarding the  breakdown happened
and power cuts  imposed on the feeders  to the  ABT control room being
 functional at  each circle  level.
2. The ABT cell will convey regarding the breakdown to the concerned JE/AFM
in charge and will ascertain the likely time which will be taken in attending
the breakdown.
3. On receipt of both the information’s, the ABT cell  will immediately  convey
regarding the  breakdown/power cut on 33/11 KV  effected feeder  to call
centre of UHBVN/DHBVN along with its likely time of restoring power
supply.
4.  In response to this, call centre will accordingly, intimate the
 breakdown / power cut of that feeder and effected area of that feeder to
the complainants. If any complaint is received at the call centre regarding
electricity supply failure of that area.
5. SE (OP) concerned  will monitor  whether  this information / data is being
supplied  by the  Sub – Stations ( UH/HVPN) to the  ABT cell  and thereafter
to the  call centre time to time.

20.19 Removal of cable, meter and other equipment (MCB) from consumers
premises while effecting PDCO. (Sales Instruction No.U-24/2013)

Please refer to SI No.U-02/2005 vide which it was directed that meter, cable and other
equipment be removed but it has come to the notice that the instructions are not
complied with, which has been viewed very seriously by the management.
 As such, the matter has again been reviewed and decided that while effecting the
PDCO, meter, cable and MCB must be removed from the site and taken in CA-21-22 &
CA-104. CA/ UDCR are hereby directed not to enter the PDCO in the record till the CA
21/22 and CA 104 Entry No. found recorded on the PDCO.
It is also made clear that if a premises is locked for more than 6 months then the
PDCO be effected by disconnecting cable from outside. The SDO shall maintain a
separate register for such cases and review the same.
 SI No.U-02/2005 and other on the subject are superseded.
‘This sales circular does not infringe (directly or indirectly) any part of the
tariff order issued by the Commission.’

20.20 Delta Change Management in Consumer Indexing (Sales Instruction No.U -

As 100% consumer indexing is going to be completed very s hortly and 18 digits

code in the consumer data base, it becomes very essential that any change occurring

Page | 666

with reference to the information regarding Sub-station Change, f eeder change,
Distribution Transformer change etc. is incorporated in the consumer base data during
and after completion of consumer indexing.
 To overcome, the issue of managing exact consumer base data the following
procedure and check points have been d esigned which are to be followed strictly in
updating the consumer data as well as for calculating the exact energy accounting and
calculation of AT&C losses.
A.  Delta changes in consumer indexing required in the following
 cases:-
a. Existing HT / LT Line extension.
b. Change of LT Supply from one DT to other due to augmentation /
installation of additional DT.
c. Shifting of Consumer from one DT to other DT or one feeder to other
feeder due to augmentation of conductor/ cable and change in
alignment of HT / LT Line.
d. The above changes will be intimated in the format as under:-

Format 1 has to be filled in at the time of sanction of estimate, drawing of material,

20.21 Reporting of electrical accidents. (Sales Circular No. U-02/2013)

Please refer to  SC No.U -03/2008 dated 10.01.2008 vide which new
formats for reporting of electrical accident cases of Human being and live stock and the

Page | 667

investigation reports was circulated for implementation by the field offices. Further, field
offices were directed to prepare and forward it to the competent authority on the
enclosed proformas i.e., Annexure-I and Annexure-2.
Now, in pursuance of Haryana State Litigation Policy - 2010 and Indian
Electricity Rules – 1956, Section 44 (A), to curb litigation and to save Nigam from
litigation expenses like Advocate’s fee TA/DA etc. and to ascertain exact cause of
electrocution i.e., on Nigam’s System or on consumer’s installation, all electrical
accident cases and their investigation reports should be prepared and forwarded to the
competent authority by the SDO/OP on the formats already specified. In the event of
electrocution on Nigam’s installation the concerned person will report to SDO/OP within
24 hours of the accident with a copy to Chief Electrical Inspector, Haryana failing which
no case shall be entertained by the Nigam for which wide publicity may be done through
public notices etc. by the field officers.
A committee of concerned SE/OP, XEN/OP & SDO/OP has been
constituted to settle this type of Electrocution cases  by way of giving compensation
through Open Darbars.
SC No.U-03/2008 is superseded.
The above instructions should be brought to the notice of all concerned for
careful and meticulous compliance.

20.22 Safety measures to minimize accidents ( Sales Instruction No.U-07/2012)
In compliance to the HERC order on ARR for FY 2012 -13 dated 31st March, 2012. The
matter has been deliberated and found that safety measures are not being followed
thereby causing avoidable accidents.
Further, it has been noted with concern that the number of fatal and nonfatal
accidents involving human beings (Nigam employees & private persons) and animals are
on increase. It appears that no step are being taken to reduce accidents.
All SEs (OP) are directed that they should provide proper training to their
employees regularly on the equipment being handled by them and  on various safety
measures to be followed while working on the equipment. All the technical employees
who are handling the equipment should be provided with proper safety kits. The
distribution system should also be maintained and protected properly in li ne with the
provisions of CEA Regulations on ‘Provision relating to Safety and Electricity supply’.
It must be ensured that cut outs/LT fuse units provided on various
poles/structures are mounted at appropriate height should not touch human being and
animals so that these are inaccessible and further that these cut outs/LT fuse units
should conform to specification of the BIS or International Electro Technical
Commission. However action taken report/progress made may be supplied by 30th June,
2012

20.23 Distribution Line Losses (Sales Instruction No. U-18/2011)

In continuation to SI No. U -11/2011, issued vide Memo No. Ch -
178/RG265/AT&C Losses/C-II dated 7.02.2011 for Distribution Line Losses.
It has further been decided that Clause g) of SI No. U-11/2011 may be read as under:-
“To streamline the difference of System Operation & Commercial for accounting of
distribution losses/AT&C losses, it is proposed to ascertain distribution/AT&C losses
for a particular month in which the billing, Revenue Assessment and Reve nue
Realization for the units received in the previous month are accounted.
e.g to calculate Distribution & AT&C losses for particular month say Feb. 11, the receipt
for the month of Jan. 11 and billing, Revenue Assessment and Revenue Realization for
the month of Feb.11 shall be taken”.
All other terms and conditions of Sales instruction No U -11/2011 shall remain
unchanged.
20.24 Calculation of AT & C losses (Sales Instruction No. U- 15/2011)
While calculating the A.T & C losses, the amount of surcharge levied is also being taken
into account. Since the amount of surcharge is not related to the units billed/realized
and as such it should not be accounted for as part of assessment/realisation (revenue).
The calculation of A.T&C losses is meant to find out the dif ference between the units
purchased and units realised. The amount of surcharge is not related to either units
billed or units realised. It is finance charges in the nature and not part of sale of power.
After deliberations, it has been decided that for the purpose of calculating A.T&C
losses, the amount of surcharge assessed or collected/realised should not be taken into
account.

20.25 Periodic Inspection of substations and feeders and maintaining feeder wise
energy data (Sales Instruction No. U- 06 /2011)
High loss level of 11 kV feeders has been a matter of concern for the Nigam. To monitor
line losses it has been decided that the SDO/XEN/SE/CE at the field levels shall
periodically inspect/visit the substations and feeders in their area of jurisdiction.
The frequency of visits to substations of different field officers is given below:

Page | 672

Sr. No. Field Officer Frequency of visit to Substation
1 CE Should visit at least one substation in two
months
2 SE Should visit at least two substations in a
month
3 XEN Should visit at least one substation per two
week
4 S.D.O. Should visit at least one substation per week

Respective CE/SE shall be responsible for monitoring the above activity.
During the visits the officers are required to analyze the feeder wise energy data
so that the causes of very high level of technical and commercial losses could be
identified. Accordingly, short- and long-term remedial measures should be planned and
implemented to control the same.
Also, the SDO’s should maintain the feeder-wise energy data (i.e. energy sent out
from the substation and total energy billed) for all the feeders under his jurisdiction of
operation.
The detailed information regarding the visit to the substation, reasons for losses
and remedial measure s taken for reducing these losses should be submitted to the
Nigam by the CE(OPs) and SE(OPs) on monthly basis

20.26 Distribution Line Losses (Sales Instruction No. U- 11/2011)

As the distribution line losses are being calculated differently in various offices so the
matter was discussed in ORC dated 08.01.2011 and decided as under. The LT side
interface meter reading (units) comparing with check meter installed at same
installation on the power transformer should be taken. This is mandatory to be checked
by SDO under whose jurisdiction the substation is located and should be
checked/verified by the XEN concerned.
a) In case of 33 KV substations the 11 KV incoming meter reading w ill be treated as
input for sub-division/division.
b) The difference between 33 KV Interface meter installed at HVPN substation and
incoming 11 KV at UHBVN end, the difference between interface & 11 KV incoming are
accountable as sub-transmission losses.
c)
i) 11 KV incoming meter reading at 33 KV substation and sum of all outgoing feeders is
to be seen and matched by distributing the difference equally (which may with plus or
minus sign depending upon accuracy of meters). This will supply to all voltage  level
substations equally.
ii) In case of 33 KV S/Stn, the 11 KV incoming meter consumption will be treated as
Input receipt of the S/Divn. The difference between the consumption of 11 KV incoming
& total of all outgoing feeders at that substation should be nominal i.e. about+1%. If the
difference is more than the above limit, the same should be investigated immediately by
the concerned SDO/XEN. On HVPN S/Stns, it should be carried out by the concerned
SSE/XEN TS HVPN.
d)
i) In the case of independent feeder, the billing should be done on the sending end meter
i.e. emanating substation end of the feeder meter by the field officer concerned. In case
the S/Stn. feeder meter is defective the billing will be done at consumer end and the

Page | 673

defective meter will be set right immediately. In case of difference of consumption
between sending end meter and consumer end meter higher of two will be taken and
meters duly calibrated.
ii) Keeping in view HERC direction i.e. HERC/12/2005 Sales Circular 36/2009 Clause-
2 should be taken care and consumer end meter should be got set right immediately.
Clause-2 of Sales Circular U-36/2009 “Therefore, in such cases, the consumption of the
energy be recorded from the energy meter installed at the consumer premises. However
for energy audit purpose, the consumption recorded by the substation meter and the
energy recorded by the energy meters at the consumer premises be compared.”
e)
i) In case of intermingling feeder i.e. inter -sub-division/division/circle shall be sorted
out by the respective XEN/SE’s in consultation with next higher authority if need be.
However, all out efforts shall be made that there is no intermingling and the feeders are
segregated (Separated out at S/Divn. boundary) in the future.
ii) In case of e(i) all the import/export units of all circles shall be sent to GM/SO clearly
indicating name of Substation/Feeder/Sub -Division & Division alongwith line losses
statement. iii) The import/export units should be signed by sending/accepting ‘OP’
Circle SE. The resp onsibility of getting signed shall lie with sending end
Subdivision/Division/Circle.
f) The readings recorded in the Energy Centre, HVPN, Panchkula should match with,
the readings being recorded in the field at various voltage levels substation at
00:00/24:00 of 1st and last day of month.
g) To streamline the difference of System Operation & Commercial for accounting of
distribution losses/AT & C losses, it is proposed to ascertain distribution/AT & C losses
for a particular month, the receipt during the month shall be compared with billing,
Assessment and Revenue Realization of the next month.
This supersedes all the instructions issued earlier on the subject.

20.27 Line losses for Industrial and Independent Feeders (Sales Instruction No. U-
35/2010)

On reviewing the line losses of feeders, it has been observed that the losses of
some of the Industrial and Independent Feeders have been found abnormal. The matter
was also deliberated with SE’s operations/XEN’s ‘OP’s/ SDO’s ‘OP’.
It has been decided that for c alculating the losses of the Industrial and
Independent Feeders following instructions may be followed :
1. Feeder’s wise ledgers of Industrial Feeders should be maintained.
2. Industrial and Independent Feeders should be properly classified as per
Nigam’s Instruction issued vide S.I No. U-27/2007 and S.C U-30/2009
respectively.
3. Separate metering equipment at Sub-stations for all existing Industrial &
Independent feeder should be installed at Nigam’s cost, where these have
not been provided. For prospective consumers the metering equipment will
be supplied by the prospective consumers.
4. The line losses of the Industrial & Independent feeders should be based on
actual date of reading and reading date of feeder meter & consumer meter
must be same. The readings of all the connections existing on Industrial
feeders should be taken on the same date.

Page | 674

5. The consumer end meter in case of Independent feeder should be defined as
check meter and Sub-station meter should be main meter. The difference of
two should also be indicated in the line losses statement separately.
6. Load of the Independent feeder should not be shifted on another feeders or
vice versa in any case.
7. The M&P should check both the meters of the Independent feeders on the
same date.
8. The feeder wise line losses statement of Industrial & Independent feeder
should be submitted separately duly signed by the XEN Operation and
counter signed by the SE ‘OP’ to SE/System Operation & Energy Audit.
9. The RA party should carry out the monthly Energy Audit of the Industrial &
Independent feeders.

20.28 Hiring of Nigam’s poles for laying cable TV Network and internet wires by
small cable operator and telecom operator (Sales Circular No.U-47/2007)

The feedback has been received from the field that laying of cable of TV network
and Internet wires by small cable operator and telecom operator may not be
allowed on the electric poles due to the following reasons.
1. These cables are obstacle for the staff climbing on the poles for removing the
faults etc. and sometime it beco mes the cause of electrical accidents to the
staff due to leakage.
2. These cables are also obstacle to the installation of energy meters being
installed on poles.
3. These cables also give ugly look to the electrical network as these create the
mess.
4. The income due to hiring of poles is also very meager and the same is also not
deposited by the many operators and it invites unnecessary audit
observations.
5. New cable connections are added from time to time and proper accounting of
poles is not up dated due to lack of survey by field staff.
6. It has also been experienced that it is direct interference/entanglement of the
private persons with Nigam’s system.
7. There is danger of accident to private person climbing Nigam’s pole on behalf
of cable operator and telecom operators.

In view of the above, management of the Nigam has reviewed the matter and
it has been decided as under:
1. Laying of these cables for TV and internet network on Nigam’s poles shall not
be allowed in future.
2. The balance amount of the cable operators who have already deposited the
rent for the year 2007 -08 shall be returned along with the notice of fifteen
days for removing the cables from the poles of the Nigam.
3. All XENs (OP) shall report compliance of the instructions within 30 days  of
issue of circular after removing all legal/illegal cable network of TV and
telecom operators.

This supersedes sales circular No.U-5/2007 dated 29.01.2007, U-19/2007
dated 6.3.07 and U-20/2007 dated 14.3.2007 on the above subject.

Page | 675

20.29 Loading of Distribution transformers. ( Sales Circular No.U-1/2007)

In view of large-scale damage of distribution transformers in the field, erstwhile
HSEB had fixed a ceiling of 80% load on the distribution transformers.
The matter has been reviewed in view of high rate of damage  of distribution
transformers in the field and it has been decided to restrict the load on the distribution
transformers in the field to 70%.
Accordingly, in the 1st phase, all new transformers to be added in the system shall
be loaded only upto 70% of the  rated capacity. No existing transformers should be
loaded beyond 70% by releasing new connections.
In the second phase, all distribution transformers, currently loaded beyond 70%
should be brought down to 70% by adding additional transformers/ augmentatio n of
the existing transformers. This work shall be completed by 31.3.2008 positively in the
entire UHBVN.
 The above instructions should be brought to the notice of all concerned for careful
and meticulous compliance.

20.30 Ban on use of phase changer in case of three phase supply consumers (Sales
Instruction No.U-09/2006)
It has come to the notice of the Nigam that some three phase consumers make provision
of phase changer switch in their fitting either to keep total load on one phase or to change load
of one phase to another phase whenever, supply fails on one phase. This results into overloading
of transformer on one phase causing its damage. There is no provision of phase changer either
in the Electricity Act-2003 or in the test report submitted by the consumer.
  To overcome this problem, Nigam has decided to ban the use of phase changer in
the fitting of three phase consumers. If during checking of premises, use of Phase changer is
noticed, he shall be served with a notice to remove phase changer within 48 hours failing which
his supply shall be disconnected. In case of non -compliance of notice by the consumer, his
supply shall be disconnected and shall be restored only after removal of phase changer and an
undertaking to this effect that he will not install phase changer in future. In case of subsequent
default, his supply shall be disconnected immediately without giving any notice and will be
restored only after 7 days on giving affidavit to the above effect.
  An intensive checking should be carried o ut by field staff to remove phase
changers before and after the meters.

20.31 Method of Power line crossing of Railway Tracks (Sales Instruction No. U -
31/2005)
Chief Electrical Engineer, N.W. Railway HQ office Jaipur have issued instructions to be followed
rigidly regarding method of power line crossing of railway tracks.
  In accordance with the provision of clause No.7 of regulations for power line
crossings of railway track, all low, medium and high voltage up to and including 11 KV crossing
shall normally be done by means of underground cable only while the voltage higher than 11 KV
crossings may be overhead or underground.
  It is observed that due to maintenance problem, guard wire of crossing span get
damaged and become loose after lapse of time/ageing, resulting breakage of guard wire and thus
disruption of rail traffic. It is therefore decided that henceforth, all the new and modified power
line crossings of railway track up to and including 33 KV shall be done by means of underground
cable only. However, the existing 33 KV overhead crossings will continue

20.32 Levy of departmental charges on Deposit Works. ( Sales Circular No
U-35 /2004)
  Whenever a deposit work is carried out on behalf of a consumer/
person/institution etc. estimat es are prepared indicating details of cost of material,

Page | 676

labour etc. As per the existing policy based on PWD accounting system, departmental
charges amounting to 24% are levied on the cost of estimate.
  However, the levy of departmental charges has been ex empted in respect
of the following categories by the Nigam from time to time :
1. An industry or a group of industries seek an independent feeder having their total
connected load of 1 MW or more (S.C. U-6/2003 dated 30.1.2003).
2. For shifting of 11 KV and 33 K V lines which are passing over the houses of the
residents (S.C. U-29/2003 dated 17.7.2003).

Some of the Religious Societies/Charitable Trusts have represented that
the 24% Departmental charges should not be levied as they are doing Social Work &
meeting with all the expenses which are to be incurred for laying of independent feeder.
After taking into account the request of these Religious Societies/
Charitable Trusts, the Nigam has decided as under :
1. The Religious Societies/Charitable Trusts, who are engaged in community/ social
service shall also be exempted from levy of departmental charges. The exemption
will be given after seeking the approval of SE(OP) in each case provided the
Society desires to have an independent feeder and who are willing to pay the
entire cost of construction of the independent feeder subject to the condition that
it is a bulk supply category connection.
2. All other cases which are not covered as above, the departmental charges will be
levied @ 10% instead of the prevailing rate of 24%.
It is also clarified that wherever the amount has already been paid by the
Society, the case for the refund of the amount will not be opened.
The above instructions may be brought to the notice of all concerned for careful and
meticulous compliance.

20.34 Feeder wise Line Losses (Sales Instruction No. U-16/2013)
In compliance to the HERC order dated 31.03.2013 on Distribution and Retail
Supply Business and Tariff for FY 2013-14 implemented vide SC No.U-10/2013 wherein
billing of HT/LT  (50 to 70 kW) consumers is on the basis of kVAh & for all other
categories on kWh basis.
It has come to the notice that the units received from the S/Stn. are in kWh
whereas the units billed for HT/LT consumers is on the basis of kVAh. Also, in case of
Urban / mix urban feeders, where the units billed for some of the consumers are on the
basis of kWh and on the basis of kAVH for others and the S/Divns. are manipulating
the Line Losses statement by not converting the kVAh into kWh.
The matter has been considered and decided that 0.9 power factor may be taken
into account for converting the kVAh into kWh.

20.35 Mode of payment of bills by consumer (Sales Circular No. U- 81/2006)
The existing practice of cash collection at sub -divisional cash collection
counters of the Nigam have been reviewed by the Nigam and following
amendments/instructions have been made in the existing practice of  cash collection.

(a) Cash Collection Timing: - For the purpose of payment of electricity bills by the
consumer, the Nigam’s cash collection counter shall remain open from 9.00 AM to
3.00 PM with half an hour break from 1.30 PM to 2.00 PM on all the working days.

(b) Uninterrupted Supply: - It should be ensured that the computers provided for
cash collection are equipped with UPS in working condition to avoid any loss of
data and in case where there is a problem of frequent load shedding, the cash
collection centers be provided with inverters, the sanction of which have already
been conveyed by Deputy Secretary/Technical, UHBVNL, Pa nchkula vide his
office memo no. Ch-33 /DST-18 / cash dated 18.10.2005.
